title: setMigrator has no lifecycle gate and can be rotated while a migrator holds users' parked ERC1155
description: `depositFor` is `onlyMigrator`, so rotating the pointer immediately bricks the old migrator's `migrateIn`. Parked stake can then leave only via `claimTimedOut`, which returns STAKE ONLY and drops the user out of the pool with no re-accrual and no automatic re-entry. The new migrator cannot reach the parked ERC1155 either — it sits behind the `totalParked` floor enforced by `rescueERC1155`.
impact: Principal is never lost. Parked stake becomes orphaned: depositFor is onlyMigrator, so rotating the pointer immediately bricks the old migrator's migrateIn. Parked stake can then leave only via claimTimedOut, which returns STAKE ONLY and drops the user out of the pool with no re-accrual and no automatic re-entry. The new migrator cannot reach the parked ERC1155 either — it sits behind the totalParked floor enforced by rescueERC1155.
attackPath: 1. A migration is in flight; migrator A holds N users' parked ERC1155.
2. Owner calls setMigrator(B) — ungated by poolState or by totalParked.
3. A's migrateIn now reverts (onlyMigrator on the staker side).
4. B cannot reach the ERC1155 held by A.
5. Users recover stake via claimTimedOut, losing re-accrual and their place in the pool.
likelihood: low — requires an owner rotation mid-migration, which is not a routine step.
assumptions: A migration is in progress with parked custody outstanding.
justification: Low, and bounded honestly: principal is never lost, claimTimedOut always returns stake, and the rotation is fully reversible before any timeout elapses. migrator = address(0) mid-migration is likewise non-terminal (permissionless userMigrate and emergencyWithdraw remain). The harm is lost yield-continuity and an unplanned manual re-entry, not asset loss.
recommendation: Gate setMigrator on poolState != Migrating, or on totalParked == 0.
